newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rejects peace talks in Kenya - radio.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rejects peace talks in Kenya - radio.

text.p: Zaire said on Monday it would not attend regional talks in Nairobi on the fighting and refugee crisis in its eastern borderlands.

State radio said the government had reiterated its position it would not negotiate until Rwandan troops it accuses of aggression left eastern Zaire where the Zairean army is battling ethnic Tutsi rebels.

"Zaire will not participate in discussions in Nairobi so long as a part of its territory is occupied by the aggressor," the radio said. "The government has reaffirmed this position which has already been announced previously."
Earlier an official in Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo's office said the cabinet was meeting to decide if Zaire would be represented at Tuesday's summit in Kenya.
Kenya said on Thursday President Daniel arap Moi would meet the leaders of Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Rwanda, Ethiopia and Cameroon to discuss the Zaire conflict.
Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated government denies it has troops in eastern Zaire where the Zaire army has lost a string of towns to ethnic Tutsis who say they are resisting attempts to expel them.
Fighting since last month has dispersed more than a million Hutu refugees sheltering in Zaire over the past two years after fleeing ethnic violence in Rwanda or Burundi.
